clue.text: College sandwich with meat

parts.note: wad is British slang for a sandwich or bun
ham is a cured meat

explanation.surface: A student's lunch order: a sandwich with meat at college.
explanation.walkthrough: WAD is old British army slang for a sandwich; WADHAM is a college of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Wadham is one of the constituent colleges of Oxford University, so it is an example of a college.

clue.text: Clown stops home for missionary

indicators.note: stops means plugging a gap, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an auguste is a type of circus clown
in means at home

explanation.surface: A clown halts at a house belonging to a missionary.
explanation.definitionFit: St Augustine of Canterbury was the missionary sent to convert the English in 597.

clue.text: Curiously, eighth's top

indicators.note: curiously means in an odd way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strangely, the eighth one is the best.
explanation.definitionFit: Highest means uppermost, which is what top means as an adjective.

clue.text: Call from farm's high ground falling short

indicators.note: falling short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a moor is an area of high open land

explanation.surface: A sound from a farm on the uplands that doesn't carry far.
explanation.definitionFit: A moo is the lowing sound made by a cow, a typical farmyard call.

clue.text: Servant organised group of setters

parts.note: setters are a breed of gun dog, so setters are dogs
a body is an organised group of people, as in a governing body

explanation.surface: A servant arranges a group of people who set crosswords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setters' tempts towards crossword compilers, but it means the gun dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody is a drudge who does menial work for others, a lowly servant.

clue.text: Base to remove from container?

definitions.meaning: a military or supply base is a storage station
read as ..., to take out of a pot

explanation.surface: A base used for unpacking things.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a base or storage station, and humorously means to take a plant out of its pot.

clue.text: Push the boundaries in sex — marry badly

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: gender means sex

indicators.note: badly means the word is mangled, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frivolous line about pushing limits in sex and making a poor marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a remark about sex and marriage; 'Push the boundaries' is literal, about redrawing electoral districts.
explanation.definitionFit: To gerrymander is to manipulate electoral district boundaries for political advantage.

clue.text: Huge effort to overcome old prejudice

indicators.note: to overcome is read as to come over, so the pieces surround the letter

parts.note: big means huge
a try is an effort or attempt

explanation.surface: A great effort to defeat long-held bias.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigotry is intolerant prejudice against those with different views.

clue.text: Fail to move Spaniard

parts.note: to die is to fail, as an engine dies
to go is to move

explanation.surface: A man from Spain who can't relocate.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego is a common Spanish male name, so it can stand for a Spaniard.

clue.text: Cohort mature in two ways, but lacking wife

parts.note: to mature is to age

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to mature is also to grow up

explanation.surface: A group of people who have grown older together, minus a spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mature in two ways' supplies two synonyms; 'lacking' removes W from GROWUP, leaving GROUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort is a set of people born in the same period, which is an age group.

clue.text: In a wig designed for heavy use

definitions.meaning: rug is slang for a wig, so one wearing it is jocularly ...
... equipment is sturdy and built to take punishment

explanation.surface: A hairpiece built to withstand hard wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugged means tough and robust, and humorously describes someone wearing a rug, a slang hairpiece.

clue.text: Alternative, say, to the op?

indicators.note: alternative means another arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether there is another treatment instead of surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative' rearranges SAY TO THE OP, and the whole clue describes a form of alternative medicine offered instead of an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteopathy is a manipulative form of alternative medicine, which a patient might choose instead of surgery.

clue.text: Excite pity, sharing sore throat

indicators.note: excite means stir up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Arousing sympathy by sharing one's sore throat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharyngitis is inflammation of the pharynx, the medical name for a sore throat.

clue.text: God carried by giant horse

indicators.note: carried by means the letters are borne inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A deity transported on a huge steed.
explanation.definitionFit: Thor is the Norse god of thunder, an example of a god.

clue.text: Handle success that brings in pounds

indicators.note: brings in means the letter for money is placed inside the success word

parts.note: a hit is a success, such as a hit record
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A handle on a profitable venture that earns money.
explanation.definitionFit: The hilt is the handle of a sword or dagger.

clue.text: Revelation in a topical piece shortly penned by poet

indicators.note: penned by means enclosed by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American poet

indicators.note: shortly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean song often commenting on topical events

explanation.surface: A revelation found in a timely article written by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: A calypso is a Caribbean song that often comments on current events, hence 'topical piece'.
explanation.definitionFit: Revelation, the last book of the Bible, is also called the Apocalypse; both mean a disclosure of hidden things.

clue.text: It hurts English to be down

parts.note: ow is an exclamation of pain

explanation.surface: Feeling low is painful for an Englishman.
explanation.definitionFit: To owe is to be in debt, i.e. to be down by a sum.

clue.text: Trunk on a sort of oak is capital

parts.note: a stock is the trunk or main stem of a tree
the holm oak is an evergreen oak

explanation.surface: A tree trunk on an oak tree is great.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockholm is the capital city of Sweden.

clue.text: Chalk cliffs here are killing — hurting inside

indicators.note: inside means one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to behead is to kill by decapitation
achy means hurting or aching

explanation.surface: A violent scene at the cliffs where people are being killed and hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: BEACHY HEAD is a chalk headland on the East Sussex coast of England; 'here are' is a link joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Beachy Head is the famous chalk sea cliff near Eastbourne, the highest in Britain.

clue.text: Show aggression to driver take a knife to him?

definitions.meaning: to carve someone up is to cut in front of them dangerously on the road
to carve someone up is literally to slash them with a knife

explanation.surface: Road rage escalating into stabbing a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Carve up means both to cut in on another vehicle and to slash someone with a blade.

clue.text: Pig drinking new form of water

indicators.note: drinking means taking something inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A pig drinking a novel kind of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is frozen water falling as crystals, so it is one form water takes.

clue.text: Standing across river in cloud

indicators.note: across means stretched over, so the river letter sits inside

parts.note: status means standing or rank

explanation.surface: Standing beside a river under the clouds.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a type of low, flat, grey cloud layer.

clue.text: I don't like that king, an uncultured man

parts.note: boo is an exclamation of disapproval
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: Someone disapproving of a monarch they find coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: A boor is a rude, ill-mannered person lacking refinement.

clue.text: Rounded character with stern reputation

parts.note: O is a round-shaped letter
dour means stern and severe

explanation.surface: A plump, severe-looking person with a reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: Odour as reputation comes from phrases like 'in bad odour', meaning in disfavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Odour can mean repute or standing, as in being in good or bad odour with someone.

clue.text: Make all-or-nothing effort, but smashed after attack

indicators.note: after places the smashed word following the attack word

parts.note: to go for someone is to attack them
broke is a past form meaning smashed

explanation.surface: Giving everything, but crushed following an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: To go for broke is an idiom for risking everything on one big attempt.

clue.text: See me wrapped up warmly, but showing a bit of leg

indicators.note: wrapped means enclosed, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: fur is warm clothing, so being warmly dressed is to be in fur

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Look at me bundled up, yet with a bit of leg on show.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' turns the word from bottom to top; 'See' and 'but showing' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The femur is the thigh bone, a part of the leg.

clue.text: Second in importance

definitions.meaning: a second is a very short time, an instant
something of great ... is of great significance

explanation.surface: Being the runner-up in significance.
explanation.definitionFit: A moment means both a brief instant and significance, as in a matter of moment.

clue.text: Body in the bath house, not at first for very long

parts.note: the revolutionary Jean-Paul Marat was murdered in his bath

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A corpse found in a bathhouse, left for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: The famous painting The Death of Marat shows the French revolutionary dead in his bath.
explanation.definitionFit: Marathon is used adjectivally for anything extremely long-lasting, as in a marathon session.

clue.text: Fabulous bird, not quite a stone

indicators.note: not quite means the word is left one letter short

parts.note: a rock is a stone

explanation.surface: A mythical bird that is almost a stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant mythical bird from Arabian legend.

clue.text: Member of XV a failure taking line out, I suggest

parts.note: a prop is a forward in a rugby union team of fifteen

indicators.note: taking with out means removing, so a letter is extracted
out completes the instruction to remove the letter

parts.note: a loser is a failure

explanation.surface: A rugby player, a flop, removes a line from a proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: XV is a rugby union team; 'taking line out' removes L from LOSER, leaving OSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposer is the person who puts forward a motion, saying in effect I suggest.

clue.text: A Wagner opera's short title, but in Italian

parts.note: Mozart's opera Cosi fan tutte is commonly called Cosi
ma is the Italian word for but

explanation.surface: Describing the abbreviated name of a Wagner opera, with a twist into Italian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Wagner opera' looks like one phrase, but the definition is just 'A Wagner': Cosima, Richard Wagner's wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosima Wagner was the wife of the composer Richard Wagner, so she was one of the Wagner family.
